text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout id=canary-2026-03-21-17 flagged: p95 latency > 500ms in us-west-2 for 6m. Suggested action: hold traffic split. auto-rollback = OFF (safety_valve counts = 2). link: https://telemetry/redwood/canary-2026-03-21-17
Maya: saw it, looking at frontend logs and kernel metrics now. ETA 8m.
AJ: +1 on hold. curious why auto-rollback didn’t trigger — what are the thresholds?
deploy-bot: Auto-rollback rules: requires >=3 infra alerts OR >= 10% error-rise OR safety_valve=true + sustained latency. Current: 2 infra alerts (kv-cache and kernel-queue), error rate +0.4%. No auto-revert.
Sophie: my read: this meets human-review threshold. recommend manual pin to v2.5.6 for hosted, keep dedicated pinned. OpsOnCall can you prepare cust comms and SLA note if we push rollback?
OpsOnCall: on it. Drafting short note now, will ping #customer-ops. ETA 12m. Do we want a temporary outage window?
Lee: hosted customers may see degraded latency but no request drops. No planned outage needed, but we should avoid automated re-release until we confirm root cause.
AJ: I'll run a quick bisect on the canary batch that introduced the kernel flag. If we pin, what's the exact command to pin release?
Maya: pin command (internal tool):
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/releases/pin \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"version":"2.5.6","scope":"hosted","reason":"canary_latency_regression_1768509999"}'
```
AJ: thanks. I'll stand by to execute once we confirm smoke.
Sophie: ops, include these bullets in the comms: 1) brief symptom (canary high p95), 2) action (holding rollout + pin to stable), 3) ETA for follow-up (30m), 4) customer impact (potential slow responses).
OpsOnCall: ack — posting to customers now and adding incident link.
deploy-bot: Action taken: traffic split hold applied to canary-2026-03-21-17. AuditID=rbk-abc123. No auto-rollback executed.
Maya: I ran smoke against v2.5.6 after pin in staging and infra looks stable. Ready for pin in prod.
AJ: I executed the pin command for hosted scope and confirmed pinned -> 2.5.6. Verified routing rollback to stable variant.
Sophie: Good. We'll keep canary paused for 2 hours and then attempt a constrained re-rollout (5% traffic) if telemetry is green. Add note to release notes: "Rollout to hosted paused due to p95 regression; rolled back to 2.5.6 for stability. Investigation ongoing."
Nora: product team notified — preparing customer-facing blurb for high-touch accounts.
Lee: filed follow-up ticket with infra: investigate kernel-queue backpressure pattern + KV cache TTL interaction (ticket INFRA-4721).
OpsOnCall: customer comms posted: "We observed increased latency during a canary rollout and temporarily resumed the previous stable version while we investigate. No data loss. We'll provide updates within 30 minutes." :thumbsup:
Sophie: thanks all. Postmortem checklist: assign owner (Maya), timeline, telemetry snapshots, and whether we should enable auto-rollback for this rule set.
Maya: I'll own the postmortem. Starting timeline capture now.
AJ: leaving a note in the runbook that pin=server-side command requires oncall approval unless auto-rollback triggers.
deploy-bot: Closing: canary held, prod pinned to 2.5.6, incident ticket INFRA-4721 created, customer comms sent.
Sophie: moving to #release-handoffs for follow-up ops sync. :pray:
